root_cause.text: The PN532 UART receive function continuously appends incoming bytes to a fixed-size socket buffer without checking for capacity or resetting the buffer on invalid frames, allowing an unbounded memory allocation from malformed input.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that `pn532_receive_buf()` "appends every incoming byte to dev->recv_skb and only resets the buffer after pn532_uart_rx_is_frame() recognizes a complete frame," which allows the skb to grow indefinitely until the tail limit is hit. The patch adds a check: `if (unlikely(!skb_tailroom(dev->recv_skb))) skb_trim(dev->recv_skb, 0);` to drop accumulated data once the buffer is full.

The patch adds a check: `if (unlikely(!skb_tailroom(dev->recv_skb))) skb_trim(dev->recv_skb, 0);` to drop accumulated data once the buffer is full.

candidates.rationale: Directly appends a byte to the receive socket buffer without checking capacity, enabling unbounded memory allocation from repeated malformed input.
Condition checks if the current buffer forms a valid frame; when false, no action is taken to reset the buffer, allowing continuous accumulation.
Skips any reset or error handling on invalid frames, causing the buffer to grow unboundedly as malformed bytes keep being appended.
Loop that iterates over incoming bytes, enabling multiple successive appends without any capacity check or reset between iterations.
While not directly vulnerable, this line is part of the receive function context and could be related to timeout handling; included as a plausible related statement.

vuln_statements.explanation: Directly appends a byte to the socket buffer without checking capacity, allowing unbounded memory allocation from repeated malformed input.
Condition checks if the buffer forms a valid frame; when false, no reset or error handling is performed, enabling continuous accumulation of bytes.
Skips any reset or corrective action on invalid frames, causing the buffer to grow unboundedly as bytes are appended each iteration.
Loop that iterates over incoming bytes, enabling multiple successive appends without any capacity check or reset between iterations.

This line deletes the command timeout timer; while not directly causing unbounded allocation, it is part of the receive function context and could affect timeout handling related to the vulnerability.

bic_trace_step.reason: The receive function pn532_receive_buf loops over incoming bytes and appends each to dev->recv_skb via skb_put_u8 without any capacity check. It only allocates a new SKB when pn532_uart_rx_is_frame detects a complete frame. If malformed input never forms a valid frame, the fixed-size buffer fills up and the next skb_put_u8 triggers a kernel panic. No reset or overflow handling is present.
